workload_description: Three algorithms for the same physical Hamiltonian — H2 in the STO-3G basis — built entirely from ORIQX primitives and submitted side-by-side to the ORIQX gateway. (1) A classical Restricted Hartree-Fock SCF, with the full 50-iteration fixed-point loop compiled into a single ops.fori_loop IR module so the entire SCF executes as one gateway submit per geometry; this drives a Born-Oppenheimer molecular-dynamics trajectory with central-difference forces. (2) A 1-parameter VQE on the Z2xZ2-tapered 2-qubit Hamiltonian, using ops.expv for ansatz state preparation and ops.expect for the energy observable; the variational landscape is sampled with a 21-point grid scan. (3) A thermal-ensemble computation: one ops.eigs submit returns the full molecular spectrum, then statistical-mechanical observables (Z, U, F, S, C_v) are composed classically across a 60-point temperature sweep from 6,000 to 3,000,000 K, exposing the Schottky anomaly in the heat capacity. The three algorithms expose three different operator graphs to ORIQX's planner — ops.fori_loop+ops.einsum for SCF, ops.expv+ops.expect for VQE, ops.eigs for thermal — and the planner offers three distinct Pareto frontiers, demonstrating that heterogeneous co-design is meaningful not just across hardware tiers but across algorithm choices targeting the same physics.
justification: VQE H2 preflight surfaced an 18-row Pareto frontier spanning cpu-only, six Braket simulator variants (SV1, TN1, dm1, qsim, qsim-statevec, cuquantum), and seven QPU lowerings (block-qpu-cheapest / -accurate / -green / -e1e-{2,3,4}, roi-confident / -greedy). The recommendation was cpu+sim(SV1) at 252 tu (65x faster than cpu-only at 16516 tu). During the hackathon, every Braket-simulator submit returned 'unknown error' on the backend (15+ jobs across 3 simulators, 0 successful executions), while cpu-only completed 20 of 21 grid points at 0.22 s/submit with bit-exact agreement to the classical reference. We deliberately overrode the recommendation in favour of the cpu-only path: reliability beat speed for this submission. The same module without code changes would route to the recommended simulator the moment it stabilises, and the QPU paths remain available for larger molecules where the eigenvalue cost dominates the round-trip latency. The SCF and thermal modules behaved the same: stable on cpu-only, exposing different Pareto frontiers (10 SCF options including 4 QPU variants; thermal frontier dominated by spectrum-friendly backends). The SCF L1 module traces and preflights for H2O as well, but the gateway rejected every H2O submit with an h2 protocol error due to the runtime-inputs payload exceeding an HTTP/2 frame limit (7^4 ERI tensor as JSON list-of-lists); we submitted on H2 to deliver an end-to-end-validated workload while preserving the architecture that scales to larger molecules under a future server-side ERI build.
baseline_comparison: SCF baseline is the unmodified NumPy rhf_scf from pareto/tracks/md/scf.py, called with H2 atoms in STO-3G. Reference energy at R = 0.74 A: -1.11675929 Ha. The AIMD trajectory is validated at every step against this NumPy reference with track tolerance |dE| < 1e-5 Ha. VQE baseline is the analytical eigendecomposition (np.linalg.eigvalsh) of the same 4x4 tapered Hamiltonian: FCI energy = -1.13768 Ha. The VQE grid-scan minimum is the HF energy -1.117368 Ha because the chosen X0X1/2 generator produces imaginary mixing whose expectation against the real-symmetric H cancels the |01>-|10> off-diagonal coupling; the gap to FCI of 0.0204 Ha is the textbook STO-3G correlation energy of H2 and a property of the ansatz, not a numerical error. The thermal ensemble validates against the analytical Boltzmann statistics: at T -> infinity entropy approaches ln(4) = 1.386 (max entropy on a 4-dim Hilbert), at T -> 0 the ground-state population p_0 -> 1, and the Schottky-anomaly peak in C_v sits at k_B T = 0.42 x (E_1 - E_0), matching the analytical two-level Schottky prediction.
stretch: Custom-track pitch: three algorithms (RHF-SCF, VQE, thermal ensemble), same molecule (H2/STO-3G), same physical Hamiltonian, traced from scratch with ORIQX primitives - no domain-specific kernels imported. SCF builds a 13-op fori_loop body for the full mean-field iteration; VQE builds a 2-op expv+expect circuit on the Pauli-mapped 2-qubit Hilbert space; thermal builds a 1-op eigs module that returns the full spectrum, with all temperature dependence composed classically. The thermal twist (statistical mechanics at extreme temperatures) is the explicit creativity beat - going beyond ground-state optimisation to full Boltzmann thermodynamics is rare in hackathon submissions and exposes the planner to a third distinct operator graph. All three modules also trace successfully for H2O (n_basis=7, 14-op SCF body), but the gateway rejects the H2O submits due to a payload-size limit on the runtime ERI tensor - documented in preflight_log.txt and decomposition_map.md as an architectural Pareto observation. Backend stability finding: cpu-only stable, all Braket simulators (SV1, TN1, dm1, qsim, cuquantum, qsim-statevec) returned 'unknown error' on every submit during the hackathon window; we overrode the recommended cpu+sim(SV1) in favour of cpu-only. Plots: vqe_pareto_landscape.png (VQE energy landscape) and thermal_ensemble.png (4-panel: U, S, C_v, populations vs T).
